clue.text: Stacked up when cool

definitions.meaning: gathered together into a pile or set

explanation.surface: Things were piled up once the weather turned chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamps or coins gathered are an assembled set; a person who is calm and self-possessed is also described with this word.

clue.text: View as awfully verbose

indicators.note: the word verbose is treated awfully, its letters badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A wordy text seen as dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch or notice something is to look at it.

clue.text: Bays belonging to Hardy's partner

definitions.meaning: bay trees, or wreaths of their leaves given as honours
Stan Laurel was the partner of Oliver Hardy in the comedy double act, so this is his possessive

explanation.surface: Sea inlets owned by a comedian's sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay trees are the evergreen shrub whose wreaths crowned victors; the possessive names Stan of Laurel and Hardy.

clue.text: South American bird of prey is twice as dear in Italy

indicators.note: the Italian word is written two times over

parts.note: cara is Italian for dear

explanation.surface: A Latin American raptor costs double in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged falcon of the Americas that scavenges as well as hunts.

clue.text: Academic distinction for only sixty minutes?

definitions.meaning: a university qualification such as a BA
one unit of angle is divided into sixty minutes of arc

explanation.surface: A university award earned in just an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A university award is one sense; a unit of angle comprising sixty arc minutes is the other.

clue.text: Casual office-worker with long hair-a siren

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A long-haired agency secretary is a seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alluring woman, a seductress, after the singers of Greek myth.

clue.text: Drunk has been getting Irish spirit

indicators.note: the words are drunk, their letters reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker has been getting whiskey from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a wailing female ghost foretells a death.

clue.text: All will take part, as it's healthy

parts.note: whole means all of it
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: Everyone will join in, since it is good for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is good for the body is nourishing.

clue.text: A means of making pupils come clean!

definitions.text: A means of making pupils come clean!

parts.words: A means of making pupils come clean!
parts.note: pupils here are the dark centres of the eyes, not schoolchildren, and coming clean means being rinsed rather than confessing

explanation.surface: A method for getting schoolchildren to own up to their misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup shaped to the eye socket holds lotion for rinsing the eye, washing its pupil.

clue.text: Tay sure to come to this

definitions.text: Tay sure to come to this

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made to come round into a new form

explanation.surface: The River Tay is bound to end up here.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is a Scottish river that ends in a wide tidal mouth at Dundee, so the whole clue both rearranges TAYSURE and describes where the river ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: A river's tidal mouth, where it meets the sea, is the destination every river reaches.

clue.text: Resting RAF officers are in proper accommodation

indicators.note: the word for proper gives lodging to the officers, holding them within it

parts.note: proper means real or genuine
PO is the abbreviation for Pilot Officer, so several are POS

explanation.surface: Off-duty air force officers are lodged in suitable quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the act of taking rest or repose, matching the gerund sense of resting.

clue.text: The paper carrier for cheese faces replacement

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the letters of faces are replaced in a new order

explanation.surface: A container for cheese whose sides have been swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The paper carrier' suggests a newspaper delivery boy, but it is a case for documents; 'replacement' reorders the letters of 'faces' behind the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat leather case is the bag in which office documents are carried.

clue.text: It's in style for him to be up the pole!

definitions.text: him to be up the pole

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside style

parts.note: it is, read as the word it

explanation.surface: It is fashionable for a man to climb a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Early Christian ascetics such as Simeon lived on top of pillars, so being up the pole is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic hermit who lived atop a pillar for years.

clue.text: Dogs men ever-ready to fight

definitions.meaning: a family of small hunting dogs bred to go to earth
the nickname for members of Britain's volunteer Territorial Army, part-time soldiers on call

explanation.surface: Hounds and soldiers always prepared for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's Territorial Army, its part-time reserve soldiers, were nicknamed after the dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Small breeds like the fox or Jack Russell share their name with a slang term for Territorial Army volunteers.

clue.text: His words can be found in clever, serendipitous and literary works

definitions.text: His words can be found in clever, serendipitous and literary works

indicators.note: signals a run of letters lying inside the next two words of the clue

explanation.surface: A writer whose words turn up in witty, lucky literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be found in' points to the run spanning the end of 'clever' and the start of 'serendipitous'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who writes lines of poetry is a versifier, whose words appear in literary works.

clue.text: Five signify, that's clear

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to indicate is to signify

explanation.surface: A handful of people show it is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to exonerate them, justifying their innocence.

clue.text: Always wanting a goal

definitions.meaning: lacking an end or aim, read cryptically

explanation.surface: Forever lacking any target.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever, without stopping; read as end-less-ly it is also acting without an aim.

clue.text: Threadbare insomniac?

definitions.meaning: worn so that the fabric's raised fibres are gone
jokingly, someone who never gets a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone sleepless and shabbily dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth without its pile is worn thin, and someone without a doze is humorously sleepless.

clue.text: Such a wrecker rues boat vandalism

indicators.note: the words are vandalised, their letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A destroyer regrets wrecking a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately damages machinery or plans is a wrecker.

clue.text: Enlarge organisation in the main

indicators.note: the letters of enlarge are organised afresh

explanation.surface: Expand the company, broadly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad or overall, true for the most part rather than in every detail.

clue.text: Not in the main built of wood and stone

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
ore is metal-bearing rock dug from the earth

explanation.surface: Something out of the sea built of timber and rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land is the opposite of being out at sea.

clue.text: Outdated in a woman's retainers

indicators.note: outdated is placed inside the woman's possessive

parts.note: hers means belonging to a woman
old means outdated

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned servants belonging to a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that grip or keep something in place, like cigarette or pen clips.

clue.text: An engineer has high standing in the Orient

parts.note: rank is social standing
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: An engineer is highly regarded in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rankine was a 19th-century Scottish engineer, the namesake of a temperature scale.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rankine, Scottish physicist and engineer of thermodynamics.

clue.text: Swordsman does his two times table, we hear

indicators.note: the words are judged by how they are spoken rather than written

parts.note: a double register, a dual list

explanation.surface: A fencer recites his two-times table out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in formal single combat often fought with swords.

clue.text: As it falls about it makes one laugh

indicators.note: the two words fall about, tumbling into a new order

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: As it falls over, a comedy makes one laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking work that ridicules folly through irony is meant to amuse.

clue.text: Make-up-a paler one — for flying

indicators.note: the letters are made up again into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Cosmetics to make someone look whiter, for use on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed-wing aircraft is a vehicle used for travel through the air.

clue.text: Used in days gone by for pitch lighting

definitions.text: Used in days gone by for pitch lighting

parts.words: Used in days gone by for pitch lighting
parts.note: pitch is the tar burned as fuel in an old iron basket, not a sports field under floodlights

explanation.surface: Something once used to light a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron basket of burning pitch or oil, raised on a pole, was a medieval torch or beacon.

clue.text: Retribution seems in order

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Punishment appears to be appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Greek goddess of vengeance, it means a just punishment or downfall.

clue.text: Gunmen trapped in a tradesman's vehicle

indicators.note: the gunmen are caught inside the tradesman

parts.note: a tiler is a tradesman who lays tiles
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men are holed up in a workman's van.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpowered cart towed behind a car or lorry is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Former top journalist being squeezed out

parts.note: ex means former
the press is the body of journalists
ED is short for editor, the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A former chief reporter is being pushed out of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice extracted by pressing fruit is said to be pressed out in this way.
